pattern.description: Inverse of a UI push-in: a tight close-up of the toolbar shows the Edit text button being clicked (fills orange), then the view rapidly pulls out to reveal the whole app with the editable text block selected on the canvas.
pattern.why_premium: The close-up makes a tiny toolbar click legible, and the pull-out immediately shows its consequence in context, so viewers follow cause and effect without a cursor hunt.

build_hint.gsap: tl.to('.btn-edit', {backgroundColor: '#d9775a', color: '#fff', duration: 0.08, ease: 'none'}).fromTo('.app-stage', {scale: 3, xPercent: -40, yPercent: 30}, {scale: 1, xPercent: 0, yPercent: 0, duration: 0.35, ease: 'expo.out'}, '+=0.05').to('.cursor', {opacity: 1, duration: 0.01}, '<')
build_hint.remotion: Button colour switches on the click frame (step). Stage scale = interpolate(spring({frame: frame - clickFrame - 2, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 180, mass: 1}}), [0, 1], [3, 1]) with transformOrigin at the Edit text button, so the zoom anchors on it; no overshoot.

notes: Visually this is a strong pull-out (close-up toolbar to full app over ~2 frames, f1368-f1370), while code's camera verdict is tilt_down with scale ~1.0; the scale change may be too fast/cut-like for the camera estimator. Could alternatively be a hard cut followed by a small drift. Pattern is push-in family in reverse; a human may prefer a 'ui_camera_pull_out' proposal.
